moments.title: Richardson's house for the Glessners
moments.text: Architect H.H. Richardson designed the granite house for John J. Glessner, an executive with the International Harvester Company, and it was finished late in 1887. It is Richardson's only surviving building in Chicago.

moments.title: "Like a prison"
moments.text: With walls set nearly at the property line and few windows facing the street, the house turned its back on Prairie Avenue and opened onto a private courtyard. Neighbors, among them George Pullman, disliked the rough stone, and some likened it to a prison.

moments.title: Millionaires' row fades
moments.text: Many of Prairie Avenue's Gilded Age mansions were later torn down; George Pullman's was razed in 1922 after his widow's death.

moments.title: Saved from demolition
moments.text: Preservationists saved the house from demolition, an effort that also created the group now called the Chicago Architecture Center.

moments.title: Named a Chicago Landmark
moments.text: The city designated the house a landmark, and it opened for tours in 1971.

moments.title: Today: Glessner House museum
moments.text: An independent nonprofit formed in 1994 runs the house as a museum in the Prairie Avenue Historic District.
